# Arm structural joints: C1 tie-rod joints + M1 inline roll (generated by `python -m rnd.joints`)

C1: the pitch hub → pitch tube and the yaw flange → yaw tube joints were 6 × M3 into heat-set inserts in pull-out. Both
are now **tie-rod joints**: steel or aluminium threads only, the printed tube and hub clamped in compression between
metal parts (rnd/parts/shoulder.py HUB_TIE, rnd/parts/roll.py YAW_TIE). M1: the inline GIM8108-36 output boss, its rear
screws and its hard stops.

Loads at each joint interface come from the twin (rnd/twin.py, CAD masses) as the full wrench of everything outboard of
the interface: **pull-off** N (along the joint axis, outboard), **bending** M (the prying moment, perpendicular to the
axis), **torsion** T (about the axis, carried by the double-D / hex form fit, not by the tie).
- **Basket** (R2d): the rnd/basket.py targets with the D20 motors and 4.54 kg per hand; every collision-free IK solution
  is kept (an upper bound on the planner's pick), × 1.5 dynamic.
- **Hug** (R2c, rnd/payload_study.py case B): upper arm hanging, forearm horizontal, 4.54 kg 0.30 m out along the
  forearm, yaw 0/±45°, × 1.5 dynamic.
- **Bump**: 140 N at the grasp point (R17 transient contact limit) in ±X/±Y/±Z, arm hanging / forward / abducted /
  elbow 90°, plus the arm's weight. A fault/abuse load: checked against ultimate, the joint may gap.
- **Stall**: each of pitch, roll and elbow at its peak (D20 set, the worse one) driving the hand into a rigid block (the
  block force = stall torque / lever, in the joint's direction of motion), same poses. Fault load, as the bump.

Joint model (clamp()): a rigid metal end plate (crank/clamp ring, aluminium flange) on the printed contact annulus,
which is a compression-only elastic foundation (E 1.8 GPa over the printed stack length), with the bolts/tie as springs
holding the preload. It gives the moment at which the interface starts to gap, and the bolt force and peak printed
contact stress under each case. Criteria: service (basket, hug) no gap and contact ≤ 12 MPa; fault (bump, stall) bolt
≤ proof load, thread strip ≥ 1.5 × the bolt force, contact ≤ 40 MPa (PETG compressive yield ≈ 55–60 MPa, ESTIMATE;
compression closes the layers, so the across-layer 12 MPa does not apply).

Preload over life (Neon review 2026-11-27, finding 3 / assumption 1): the flat "× 0.75 for creep" is replaced by a
creep model (life_preload(): effective modulus, creep coefficient φ bounded from printed-PETG data, + embedding + a
cold day). With it, the wave-3 joints (print as the clamped member) keep ≈ 30 % of their preload, and the yaw tie
gaps under the basket wrench. Disc springs in series (the review's fix) keep more preload but soften the bolts, whose
stiffness carried the bending (disc_alternative()): not enough. So each C1 bolt now runs in steel crush sleeves
(SleeveClamp: bolt ↔ sleeve metal stack, the print sandwiched with a light squeeze): the preload only loses its
embedding, the no-gap moment is the metal stack's, and the service rows are checked at that life preload with the
print's squeeze crept away; the fault rows at the fresh and the life preload. M1 rows (inline
GIM8108-36): output dowels with load sharing, the metal rear clamp (plate + sleeves), the two-bearing roll support
(61806 + the motor's output bearing: reactions per load case from the twin, misalignment preload), the hard stops.

## Hardware

- **Pitch hub ↔ pitch tube** (rnd/parts/shoulder.py HUB_TIE): 4 × M4 class 10.9 studs (DIN 976-1, cut to 78.8 mm) on r 15.5 at 45° + k·90°, Loctite 270 into the 7075-T6 balancer crank (tapped through 4 mm, stud end flush with its inboard face), each in two steel crush sleeves Ø7.0 / Ø4.3 (42CrMo4+QT, turned; one through the tube wall r 11–20, one through the hub, butting at the hub ↔ tube face, together 0.05 ± 0.02 mm shorter than the measured tube + hub print stack), M4 nuts (ISO 4032 class 8, Loctite 243) on a C45+QT clamp ring (was 6061-T6, Astra #3 m9) r 11–21 × 2 in a 5.7 mm recess of the detach face; 1.5 kN each (≈ 1.3 N·m, ESTIMATE). Assembly: tube into the inner wall → crank + studs from the inboard side → tube sleeves over the studs → belt → outer wall → hub over the double-D, hub sleeves → ring, nuts.
- **Yaw flange ↔ yaw tube** (rnd/parts/roll.py YAW_TIE): 7075-T6 flange (was 6061-T6: Astra #3 m9, the sleeve feet on its spigot top; its hex spigot stays the torque path). 6 × M3 × 40 ISO 4762 class 12.9 go down from the tube's top end in steel crush sleeves Ø4.6 / Ø3.2 (ring → the flange's spigot top, 0.05 mm shorter than the print), heads on a C45+QT clamp ring (was S235, Astra #3 m9) r 8.5–16.8 × 2 in a Ø34 × 5.5 counterbore (heads 0.5 mm under the top), through Ø3.4 holes in the wall into M3 threads tapped at the hex corners (r 11) of the flange's spigot + plate (8.3 mm engaged, Loctite 243); 1.2 kN each (≈ 0.5 N·m). Tightened from above on the bench, before the yaw block goes onto the roll output.
- Crush sleeves (D26 cost-down: stock tube where its guaranteed yield clears the sleeve stress, cut and faced square by the builder in a drilled guide block to the measured print − 0.05 ± 0.02, checked with a micrometer): pitch Ø7.0 / Ø4.3 42CrMo4+QT, turned (R_p ≥ 750 MPa): turned: the two sleeves butt at the hub ↔ tube face, so they must be located by the Ø7.1 hole; 1/4" × .035" 4130 (F_ty 517) floats 0.4 mm in it (butt overlap down to ≈ 0.3 of its 0.89 mm wall) and its softer section takes the stall row 1.18 → 1.08× (thread strip); it fits if the CAD hole goes Ø7.1 → Ø6.45; yaw Ø4.6 / Ø3.2 42CrMo4+QT, turned (R_p ≥ 750 MPa): turned: no stock tube ≤ Ø4.7 with an ID ≥ 3.2 clears the yaw stall stress (4.5 × 0.6 E355+SR, R_eH 440: ≈ 1.07×); rear Ø6.0 / Ø4.4 E235+C precision tube (EN 10305-1; R_eH taken as the E235+N 235 MPa floor) (R_p ≥ 235 MPa): 6 × 0.8 seamless E235+C precision tube; clevis Ø8.0 / Ø5.6 E235+C precision tube (EN 10305-1; R_eH taken as 235 MPa) (R_p ≥ 235 MPa): 8 × 1.2 seamless E235+C precision tube (press fit in the print: the bearing path). Was turned 42CrMo4+QT on all four sets ($7 each, 56 per robot); an E235 tube would yield at the pitch / yaw bump and stall rows. The review's DIN 6796 disc springs (McMaster-Carr "DIN 6796 lock washers", norelem 07000, Bossard BN 794; load to flat M3 1.32 / M4 3.77 kN) were evaluated and not used: see the preload rows.
- Not drawn (rnd/parts/arm.py, arm track): the upper bone ↔ yaw flange screws. With the flange in aluminium they should be M4 into tapped holes in the flange, heads on washers on the bone flange, not inserts.

## C1: preload over life

φ = 2.0 design / 1.0 nominal (ESTIMATE, bounded from printed-PETG creep data: Aerospace 2022 9(3) 124, PMC12349189; Findley t^n + 1–2 decades of 40–50 °C shift); PETG α 68e-6/K (datasheet range 60–70e-6, ESTIMATE) vs steel 11.5e-6, assembled at 20 °C, coldest service 10 °C; embedding 10 µm per printed interface (ESTIMATE: FDM layer peaks; VDI 2230 gives ≈ 2–3 µm per machined metal interface, used for the metal joints).

- **pitch hub ↔ tube:** 4 × M4 10.9 at 1.50 kN in Ø7.0/4.3 steel crush sleeves (69.6 mm, 69 kN/mm; the print sandwiched with a 0.05 mm squeeze ≈ 1.3 MPa that may creep away): metal stack, embedding only → life preload **1.33 kN (88 %)** vs 0.72 kN for no gap under the worst service wrench (30.2 N·m, 0 N) → **1.84×**. Before: wave 3 as designed (print as the clamped member, 1.5 kN): bolt 43 vs print 183 µm/kN per bolt (69.6 mm of PETG: 274 µm of elastic squeeze, so the springs are bolt + print, not the bolt alone), life preload 0.46 kN (30 %; φ 1: 0.66 kN) vs 0.40 kN needed → 1.13×. Not chosen: the review's disc springs (3 × DIN 6796-M4 in series, 0.28 mm travel): life 0.71 kN but the softer bolts need 0.85 kN → 0.83× (the stiff bolts carried the bending). ✅
- **yaw flange ↔ tube:** 6 × M3 12.9 at 1.20 kN in Ø4.6/3.2 steel crush sleeves (29.7 mm, 58 kN/mm; the print sandwiched with a 0.05 mm squeeze ≈ 2.4 MPa that may creep away): metal stack, embedding only → life preload **1.05 kN (87 %)** vs 0.65 kN for no gap under the worst service wrench (32.6 N·m, 102 N) → **1.61×**. Before: wave 3 as designed (print as the clamped member, 1.0 kN): bolt 36 vs print 145 µm/kN per bolt (37.7 mm of PETG: 145 µm of elastic squeeze, so the springs are bolt + print, not the bolt alone), life preload 0.30 kN (30 %; φ 1: 0.43 kN) vs 0.35 kN needed → 0.86×. Not chosen: the review's disc springs (3 × DIN 6796-M3 in series, 0.53 mm travel): life 0.68 kN but the softer bolts need 0.69 kN → 0.98× (the stiff bolts carried the bending). ✅

## C1: contact faces, clamp rings, sleeve lengths (Astra #3 major 9)

Contact pressure on each face that a bolt head, nut or sleeve end stands on, at the worst service and fault rows above, against the face's R_p (service ≤ R_p: no plastic set; fault ≤ 1.1 R_p: onset of local indentation, ESTIMATE). Sources: 6061-T6 EN 485-2 EN AW-6061 T6 plate R_p0.2 ≥ 240; 7075-T6 EN 485-2 EN AW-7075 T651 R_p0.2 ≥ 460; S235 EN 10025-2 R_eH ≥ 235; C45+QT EN 10083-2 +QT d ≤ 16 R_e ≥ 490; 42CrMo4+QT EN 10083-3 +QT R_p0.2 ≥ 750; ISO 7092 200 HV ≈ 200 HV steel washer, R_p ≈ 450 (ESTIMATE).

| Joint | Face | Area | p service / fault | Before | After | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pitch hub ↔ tube | M4 nut (d_w 5.9) on the clamp ring | 11.4 mm² | 152 / 377 MPa | 6061-T6: 0.70× ❌ | C45+QT: 1.43× | ✅ |
| pitch hub ↔ tube | sleeve end on the clamp ring | 22.6 mm² | 90 / 299 MPa | 6061-T6: 0.88× ❌ | C45+QT: 1.80× | ✅ |
| pitch hub ↔ tube | sleeve end on the 7075-T6 crank | 24.0 mm² | 85 / 282 MPa | 7075-T6: 1.79× ✅ | 7075-T6: 1.79× | ✅ |
| pitch hub ↔ tube | sleeve ↔ sleeve butt (hub ↔ tube face) | 24.0 mm² | 85 / 282 MPa | 42CrMo4+QT: 2.93× ✅ | 42CrMo4+QT: 2.93× | ✅ |
| yaw flange ↔ tube | M3 head (d_w 5.07) on the clamp ring | 11.1 mm² | 134 / 214 MPa | S235: 1.21× ✅ | C45+QT: 2.52× | ✅ |
| yaw flange ↔ tube | sleeve end on the clamp ring | 7.5 mm² | 218 / 401 MPa | S235: 0.64× ❌ | C45+QT: 1.34× | ✅ |
| yaw flange ↔ tube | sleeve foot on the flange's spigot top | 8.6 mm² | 191 / 353 MPa | 6061-T6: 0.75× ❌ | 7075-T6: 1.43× | ✅ |
- pitch hub ↔ tube: clamp ring r 11.0–21.0 × 2 between studs on the print (beam on an elastic foundation): it imposes 66% of the 0.05 mm squeeze between studs in 6061 (63 MPa), 85% in steel (82 MPa). The sleeves and the nut or head are coaxial, so the clamp load goes through the ring's thickness, not its span; only the print's light squeeze bends it, and the service rows already take that squeeze as crept away.
- yaw flange ↔ tube: clamp ring r 8.5–16.8 × 2 between studs on the print (beam on an elastic foundation): it imposes 95% of the 0.05 mm squeeze between studs in 6061 (38 MPa), 98% in steel (39 MPa). The sleeves and the nut or head are coaxial, so the clamp load goes through the ring's thickness, not its span; only the print's light squeeze bends it, and the service rows already take that squeeze as crept away.
- Squeeze, one dimension: the pitch's two sleeves per stud (tube + hub) are faced so that TOGETHER they are 0.05 ± 0.02 mm shorter than the measured tube + hub print stack (the tube sleeve to the tube print − 0.025, then the hub sleeve to the remainder, micrometer); before, each was specified 0.05 short, i.e. 0.10 in total against the model's 0.05. The yaw has one sleeve per screw: 0.05 ± 0.02 under the print, the same micrometer check.
- Unequal sleeves and preload scatter: each stud's nut closes its own bolt ↔ sleeve loop, so a ± 0.02 mm sleeve-length spread changes only the local print squeeze, not the sleeve preload. The real scatter is the tightening: a click wrench gives ± 20 % (VDI 2230 α_A ≈ 1.6, ESTIMATE). With every bolt at −20 % the service preload margins become pitch hub ↔ tube 1.47×; yaw flange ↔ tube 1.31× (no gap); a single low bolt is between that and nominal.
- Not drawn yet (arm track): the upper bone ↔ yaw flange screws, the detach clamp, the elbow core / clamp and the wrist output bearing in the same wrench chain — those rows stay open (review major 9).

- **M1 output boss ↔ 7075 adapter (torque path):** bearing allowable 150 MPa (reverted from 240: cast A380-class σ_y ≈ 160 MPa with no bearing factor, ESTIMATE until the seller names the boss material; a steel or wrought 6061-T6 boss would justify ≈ 240). 3 × Ø4 × 4 mm on r 14.25: 2.40 kN each; dowel stiffness 41 kN/mm (Huth, Ø4 steel in 4 mm Al + 7 mm 7075); the first dowel takes k·δ before the others touch: δ 8 µm (H7/m6 spread, ISO 286) when the dowels are bonded (Loctite 638) into Ø4.1 adapter holes while seated in the motor (the adapter's hole positions drop out) → 93 N·m; dry in jig-bored holes δ ≈ 40 µm (± 0.02 true position each side, ESTIMATE) → 56 N·m (the review's ≈ 55 N·m); equal sharing 103 N·m. + 3 × M4 × 10 csk at 2.0 kN, μ 0.15, metal on metal (no creep): 13 N·m (strip of 2.65 mm effective M4 in the cast boss ≈ 3.9 kN). Dowel shear 242 N·m (ISO 8734). Criterion: stall is a fault, checked at a yield-level bearing allowable at ≥ 1.0× (as bolts ≤ proof); the 7075 adapter side is 7 mm deep. The 140 N bump puts up to 113 N·m on the roll output (1.07× this capacity): below the stall only if the actuator backdrives at its current limit (open: backdrive torque, seller / bench)
- **M1 rear mount: 8 × M4 into the 3.5 mm housing threads:** stack per screw: bolt 13 + sleeve 7 + plate 1 µm/kN, 5 metal interfaces × 2 µm embedding (VDI 2230, ESTIMATE) → 70 % left, no creep term (the printed floor + cup ring are sandwiched between the plate and the motor face, sleeves -0.05 mm vs the print: located, not clamped). Friction μ 0.15 steel/Al (ESTIMATE). Engagement 25 − 22 = 3.0 mm, worst ± 0.49 (screw length js15 ± 0.42, ISO 4759-1; plate ± 0.05, sleeve ± 0.02): 2.51–3.49 in 3.5 mm, so no shim picking; strip at the shortest (2.16 mm effective) 3.2 kN vs the worst bolt 1.82 kN (1.8×; motor bearing 2330 N × 40 mm → 94 N·m on the bolt circle, under the 310 N·m that opens it, load factor 0.39). Stall reaction through the sleeves into the print: 2.7 MPa bearing (Ø6 × 19 mm, 8 sleeves). Sleeve yield (D26 stock tube): rear 6 × 0.8 seamless E235+C precision tube 139 MPa at the worst bolt vs 235 (1.69×); clevis M5 8 × 1.2 seamless E235+C precision tube (press fit in the print: the bearing path) 100 MPa at 1.5 kN + the 137 N·m worst output moment on PCD 64 vs 235 (2.34×)
- **M1 roll support: 61806 (rear) + the motor's output bearing:** reactions from the twin wrench of the roll output (the static roll stage taken off) on supports -32.5 / 36.5 mm (69 mm apart): service (basket, hug × 1.5) 61806 530 N, motor 617 N; fault (bump, stall) 1986 / 2330 N. Misalignment: the stub and the cup's driver pilot are one print (Ø75.2 pilot on the Ø75 driver, 0.1 radial) → static offset ≤ 0.25 worst / 0.15 RSS mm (pilot fit + print coaxiality 0.1 + motor 0.05, ESTIMATE); the rotating seat's own error (the clevis/arm print loop) is taken out by bonding the outer race (Loctite 660, 0.3 mm radial gap) with the arm bolted at mid-travel. Radial stiffness of the printed rear support 1.6–3.2 kN/mm (fea.md: stub 288 N → 0.13 mm, rear arm 525 N → 0.09 mm, in series; × 2 upper bound, ESTIMATE). The extra 61806 friction at 800 N is 18 mN·m (SKF μ 0.0015): it does not bind or blind the collision observer. **Deleting the 61806** (the review's option) needs the motor's output bearing to carry 119 N radial + 36.6 N·m tilting in service and 345 N + 137 N·m at a fault (about its own centre): only a crossed-roller or a preloaded pair with M0 ≥ 137 N·m qualifies. Seller question still open (output bearing type, C0, M0) — until then the 61806 stays
- **M1 roll hard stops (both ends):** F = τ / r: 1040 N at 35.1 N·m, 3049 N at stall (r 33.75, both dogs; the check puts it all on one). Contact band x 29.0–39.5 (10.5 mm) × 5.5 mm radial. Dog: cantilever from the adapter's back face, 7.25 mm to the contact centre, root 5.5 × 14.7 mm; block: from the ring top, 6.25 mm, root 7.2 × 20.4 mm; 7075-T6 σ_y 435 MPa (as the rear plate), contact against σ_y. Stop angles: blocks at 27.75…62.25°, 207.75…242.25°; contact at -16.5° / 104°. Load path: dog → block → ring → M4 × 6 ISO 10642 10.9 (8) (friction 56.4 N·m at 70 % of 1.6 kN each, the rest in shear on the M4 stress area; the Ø60.6 bore on the motor's Ø60 step pilots it) → housing; the adapter ↔ output-boss joint (row (a)) carried the stop torque before too. The printed clevis / yaw block / rear arm no longer carry the motor's stall torque into the stop. 7075 on 7075 at a rare hard-stop contact: hard-anodise both (ESTIMATE; wear coupon)
